title: Wireframe (text): Dedicated staged rollout dashboards (per-stage + region/pool breakdown + promotion/rollback annotations)
content:
Doc purpose
- Text-form wireframe for the Dedicated staged rollout dashboard(s).
- Goal: make it obvious whether a stage is healthy enough to promote, and where issues live (region/pool partition).
- Secondary: provide durable evidence + context during incident response (429 spikes, saturation, GPU health) and for change management (promotion/rollback audit trail alignment).

Primary users
- SRE/oncall (Redwood) and Dedicated operators during rollout execution
- Console team (to align UI + backend contract with observability)
- Infra/fleet team (to validate pool partitioning and headroom constraints)

Assumptions / data model (MVP)
- Every dataplane request metric has tags (allowlisted to avoid cardinality blowups):
  - dedicated_pool_id (or pool_name)
  - rollout_id
  - stage_id (stable ID, not freeform name)
  - region
  - model_id / model_version (optional, allowlisted)
  - build_id (optional)
- A rollout emits discrete audit-like events usable for annotations:
  - rollout_created, rollout_started
  - stage_promoted (from_stage -> to_stage)
  - stage_held, stage_resumed
  - rollout_aborted, rollout_rolled_back
  - force_promote, force_abort (admin-only)
- Gate evaluation emits time series + latest evaluation snapshot:
  - gate_result{gate_name, stage_id} = PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN
  - gate_observed_value{gate_name, stage_id}
  - gate_threshold{gate_name, stage_id}
  - gate_sample_size{gate_name, stage_id}
- Missing telemetry semantics: UNKNOWN (do not silently show green). UI should clearly show staleness.

Dashboard scope
- “Dedicated Pool Rollout — Overview” (one rollout/pool, multi-stage)
- “Dedicated Pool Rollout — Per Stage Deep Dive” (stage-focused, region + partition drilldown)

Global layout conventions
- Top bar: title + context + status
  - Pool: <dedicated_pool_name> (<dedicated_pool_id>)
  - Rollout: <rollout_id>
  - Current stage: <stage_name> (<stage_id>)
  - State: DRAFT | RUNNING | HELD | ABORTED | COMPLETED
  - Started at: <timestamp> ; Last action: <promotion/hold/abort>
- Global time range defaults: last 60m (with quick toggles: 15m / 1h / 6h / 24h)
- Global filters:
  - Region: All (multi-select)
  - Stage: All (multi-select)
  - Partition: baseline|candidate (if replica-partitioned; optional)
  - Request type: chat|embeddings|rerank (optional)
  - Route: /v1/chat/completions etc. (optional)
- Data freshness indicator:
  - “Metrics fresh” vs “Metrics stale (last sample: X min ago)”

============================
Dashboard 1: Dedicated Pool Rollout — Overview
============================

Row 0: “Rollout timeline + actions (read-only for dashboards)”
Panel 0.1 — Rollout action timeline (annotations band)
- A horizontal timeline with vertical markers for:
  - stage_promoted
  - stage_held / stage_resumed
  - rollout_aborted / rollout_rolled_back
  - force_* actions
- Marker label includes: actor (service vs human), reason (if provided), idempotency_key (optional), from/to stage.
- Tooltip: exact payload fields, plus link-out to audit event viewer (Console) if available.

Panel 0.2 — Current stage health summary (big tiles)
- 5 tiles showing latest gate status for the current stage:
  - Availability / error rate gate
  - Latency gate
  - Saturation/headroom gate
  - OOM / GPU health gate
  - Request drops / 429 gate
- Each tile shows: PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, observed value, threshold, window, sample size.
- If UNKNOWN: show staleness reason if known (telemetry lag, missing tags, low traffic).

Row 1: “Key SLO-ish signals (stage-aware, trend lines)”
Panel 1.1 — Request volume (RPS) by stage
- Stacked area or multiple lines: RPS{stage_id}
- Secondary overlay: stage traffic target (expected %) if available.
- Callout if effective traffic differs materially from target (e.g., canary starving capacity).

Panel 1.2 — Error rate by stage
- Lines: error_rate{stage_id} (5xx + model errors)
- Separate dotted line for “policy rejects” (429 / capacity shed) as it often spikes during partitioning.

Panel 1.3 — Latency p95/p99 by stage
- Two subplots or dual lines:
  - p95_latency_ms{stage_id}
  - p99_latency_ms{stage_id}
- Notes: p99 is noisy for low volume; include min sample size indicator.

Panel 1.4 — 429 / drop rate by stage
- Lines:
  - http_429_rate{stage_id}
  - request_drop_rate{stage_id} (router drops / circuit breaker)
- This is the panel we want on screen during suspected capacity starvation incidents.

Row 2: “Capacity + GPU health (to catch ‘canary partition starved’ class issues)”
Panel 2.1 — Queue depth / in-flight by stage (if available)
- Lines:
  - queue_depth{stage_id}
  - inflight_requests{stage_id}
- Optional overlay: autoscaler events (if Dedicated autoscaling is in play).

Panel 2.2 — GPU utilization + headroom by region (stage-filterable)
- Multi-series by region, averaged within filter:
  - gpu_utilization_pct{region}
  - tokens_per_sec{region}
- Additional “headroom estimate” metric if we have it: headroom_pct.

Panel 2.3 — OOM / restarts by stage
- Bars or lines:
  - oom_rate{stage_id}
  - worker_restart_rate{stage_id}
- Tooltip includes top OOM signatures if available (optional future).

Panel 2.4 — GPU health / node taints (fleet health)
- Lines:
  - ecc_error_rate
  - throttling_events
  - unhealthy_nodes_count
- Broken down by region, with a small table of top affected hosts only if cardinality-safe.

Row 3: “Gate result over time (so we can see flapping)”
Panel 3.1 — Gate status timeline per stage
- Heatmap-like strip per gate (rows) and stage (columns), showing PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN over time.
- MVP simplification: per stage, show “latest gate evaluation” table with last N evaluations.

Panel 3.2 — Error budget burn / promote eligibility (SRE-facing)
- If the error budget signal exists for Dedicated pool SLO:
  - burn_rate_1h, burn_rate_6h, remaining_budget
- Visual callout: “Promotion blocked by high burn” (if policy enforces it).

Row 4: “Breakdowns (fast drilldown without leaving overview)”
Panel 4.1 — Region breakdown table (current stage)
- Table columns per region:
  - RPS, error_rate, p95, p99, 429_rate, gpu_util, queue_depth, unhealthy_nodes
- Sorted by worst “promote readiness” score.

Panel 4.2 — Stage comparison snapshot (baseline vs candidate)
- For current stage: compare baseline partition vs candidate partition if replica-partitioned.
- Else (traffic % split): compare stage N vs stage N-1.
- Output: a small table with delta columns (candidate - baseline) and percent change.

============================
Dashboard 2: Dedicated Pool Rollout — Per Stage Deep Dive
============================

Purpose
- A page you open when gate fails or looks suspicious, to identify which region/partition is dragging the stage.

Stage selector
- Required variable: stage_id
- Secondary: region (All by default)

Row A: “Stage summary”
Panel A.1 — Stage definition (static-ish)
- Stage name, stage_id
- Traffic target: X% or “replicas: k of N”
- Safety constraints applied (from control plane validation): min headroom, min replicas per region, etc.
- Links (text): rollout plan resource ID, audit events for this stage.

Panel A.2 — Latest gate evidence (mirrors Console evidence model)
- Table per gate:
  - Gate name
  - PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN
  - Observed value
  - Threshold
  - Window
  - Sample size
  - Data freshness
  - Notes (e.g., “insufficient volume (<N requests)”, “metrics stale >5m”)

Row B: “Latency + errors (regional)”
Panel B.1 — p95/p99 latency by region (for stage)
- Lines per region (limit top 5 worst + “All others” to keep readable)

Panel B.2 — Error rate by region (for stage)
- Lines per region; separate series for 5xx vs model errors vs 429.

Panel B.3 — Top error codes / reasons (stage)
- Bar chart: top error categories
- MVP: coarse groupings only (timeout, OOM, overload/429, upstream, unknown)

Row C: “Capacity + saturation (regional)”
Panel C.1 — GPU utilization pct by region (stage)
Panel C.2 — Queue depth / scheduler backlog by region (stage)
Panel C.3 — Token throughput (tokens/sec) by region (stage)

Row D: “Partition comparison (if applicable)”
Panel D.1 — Baseline vs candidate: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
Panel D.2 — Baseline vs candidate: error + 429
Panel D.3 — Baseline vs candidate: saturation / queue depth
- Notes: this is where we catch “candidate partition has fewer replicas than expected” or “routing is skewed”.

Row E: “Annotations + correlation”
Panel E.1 — Promotions/rollbacks overlay on latency chart
- Same as timeline markers but overlaid directly on p95/p99 chart.
- Shows whether issues start exactly at promotion boundary.

Panel E.2 — “What changed?” checklist (manual notes)
- Text panel (not a metric): pulled from rollout plan metadata if available:
  - model_version changed?
  - runtime build changed?
  - routing policy changed?
  - quantization profile changed?
  - config knobs changed? (batching/caching)
- MVP: this can be an empty placeholder, but the wireframe reserves space.

============================
Annotation + event schema (for dashboards)
============================

Minimum annotation fields
- timestamp
- event_type (stage_promoted, stage_held, stage_resumed, rollout_aborted, rollout_rolled_back, force_promote, force_abort)
- rollout_id
- dedicated_pool_id
- stage_id (new stage if promotion)
- from_stage_id (if applicable)
- actor_type (system|user)
- actor_id (service name or user id)
- reason (string; optional but strongly recommended)

How annotations appear
- Global “timeline band” (Dashboard 1, Panel 0.1)
- Overlay markers on key charts (latency, error, 429) so oncall sees correlation immediately
- In tooltips, show a link text “Audit event: <event_id>” (actual link-out handled by Console, but dashboard should include event_id)

============================
MVP vs V2 notes
============================

MVP (beta)
- Overview dashboard + deep dive stage dashboard
- Annotations for promote/abort/hold + force actions
- Gate summary tiles (PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN)
- Region breakdown table
- Limited partition compare (only when partition tag exists)
- Strict label allowlist (avoid stage_name freeform; use stage_id)

V2
- Automatic “suspect region/partition” insights (ranked)
- Correlate with fleet events (maintenance, node drains) and include as annotations
- Add quality regression signal panels when evals are enabled (Selene/Olivia/Sana workstream)
- Add per-route breakdown (careful with cardinality)

Open questions (for follow-up)
- What is the canonical metric name(s) for queue depth / backlog in the dataplane? (Need alignment with Vikram/Emily)
- Do we have a stable “headroom_pct” definition for Dedicated pools across regions?
- What is the staleness threshold that flips gate status to UNKNOWN (5m vs 10m)?
- How do we represent multi-region promotion when one region is impaired mid-stage? (annotation needs region scope?)
- Do we need a “traffic_target_vs_actual” panel driven from routing logs? (to catch skew)

Notes to self (observability)
- Keep dashboards usable for low-traffic pools: show sample size prominently; do not over-trust p99 at low N.
- Explicitly show UNKNOWN rather than green when data is missing.
- Any table listing “hosts” must be opt-in and heavily capped; default view should be region/pool only.
